analysis.one_liner: Jindal Steel Limited (formerly Jindal Steel & Power) is an integrated steel producer with plants at Angul (Odisha) and Raigarh (Chhattisgarh), making flat and long steel products, plates and rails.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (quarter to Sept 2026) results came out on 23 October 2026: consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to roughly ₹16,700 crore and PAT rose 21% YoY to ₹771 crore, both records, but EBITDA margin slipped to about 15% from 16% a year ago. Management flagged that coking coal costs (a key input) rose further in the quarter and guided to another $20-25/tonne increase in Q3, meaning the margin squeeze is not yet over. The 192km Barbil-Angul iron-ore slurry pipeline was also commissioned this quarter, which should cut freight costs going forward.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a steel maker that has just finished a large expansion - it roughly doubled capacity at its main Angul plant - and that expansion is now showing up as genuinely higher volumes and revenue, not just better prices. The catch is that the raw material it needs (coking coal) has gotten pricier, so even as sales grow, the profit margin on each tonne is shrinking. The stock trades at a fairly rich 33 times earnings for a business earning only around 8-10% on its capital, so the market is betting the expansion pays off faster than the cost pressure bites.
analysis.quarters: Consolidated PAT: ₹1,045 crore (Q4 FY26, Mar-26) → ₹844 crore (Q1 FY27, Jun-26) → ₹771 crore (Q2 FY27, Sep-26). Revenue has kept climbing each quarter as the expanded Angul capacity ramps up, but EBITDA/tonne fell from ₹11,937 to ₹10,529 over the same stretch as coking coal costs rose. Full FY26 PAT was ₹3,361 crore (up from ₹2,846 crore in FY25), with a final dividend of ₹2/share declared. Two things to flag: different sources quote FY26 EBITDA as either ₹9,099 crore or ₹9,704 crore depending on whether a company 'adjusted EBITDA' figure or a standard operating-profit calculation is used - these are not strictly comparable and the gap has not been reconciled. Management has not explicitly flagged a comparability break in recent quarters' numbers.
analysis.performance_read: The stock closed at ₹1,039.90 on 26 Oct 2026, down 19.2% from its April 2026 peak of ₹1,286.50 - this is a genuine price decline, not a corporate-action artifact; the company's only splits (2003, 2008, 2009) are far outside this window and don't distort it. Over 1 year the stock is roughly flat (+0.72%), beating the Nifty (-12.37%) but badly lagging peer JSW Steel (+10.14%). Over 3 and 5 years it has comfortably beaten the Nifty (+62.45%/+137.04% vs +19.46%/+24.55%) and over 5 years has beaten JSW Steel too (+137.04% vs +90.93%), though it lagged JSW Steel over 3 years. One structural note: in December 2022 the company sold its power arm, Jindal Power, to a promoter-group entity for cash - this was a stake sale, not a shareholder demerger, so no shares were distributed to holders and the price series needs no adjustment for it. It does mean pre-2023 financial trends aren't comparable to today's steel-only numbers.
analysis.valuation_read: At ₹1,039.90, the stock trades around 33x trailing earnings and about 2x book value (Screener, 26 Oct 2026) - other aggregators show P/E as high as 38.5x depending on which trailing-earnings window they use, so treat the multiple as 'low-to-mid 30s' rather than a precise number. Whether this is cheap or expensive depends entirely on what you believe about the capacity expansion: the business currently earns only about 8-10% on capital (ROE 8.2%, ROCE 9.7%), so a 33x multiple is pricing in a meaningful step-up in earnings once the newly doubled Angul capacity is fully utilised and coking coal costs normalise. If that ramp-up disappoints or costs stay elevated, the current multiple would look rich rather than cheap.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is mostly volume-led: the Angul complex capacity roughly doubled (6 to 12 MTPA, taking total group capacity to 15.6 MTPA), and management is guiding FY27 sales volumes of 10.5-11 million tonnes, with revenue climbing each quarter as that capacity ramps. But the margin side is moving the wrong way - EBITDA/tonne has fallen as coking coal (an imported input, not something the company controls) has gotten more expensive. That combination - rising volumes, falling margins from a cost shock rather than pricing power - is the less durable kind of growth in a commodity business, and is worth watching into Q3 FY27.
analysis.health_read: Leverage looks manageable and improving: net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.51x in Q2 FY27 from 1.71x the prior quarter, and net debt/equity is a modest 0.32. Both CARE and ICRA upgraded the company's credit rating to AA+ in mid-2026, citing the capacity ramp-up. Whether profits are converting cleanly into cash - Not verified, check operating cash flow versus PAT on Screener. The more pressing risk right now looks like business risk (coking coal cost cycle, execution of the capacity ramp-up) rather than financial/balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters held 62.71% as of the September 2026 quarter, with FIIs at 8.75% and DIIs at 19.70%. Promoter share pledging is low and has been falling - a June 2026 disclosure showed the promoter entity Beaufield Holdings released pledges to bring encumbrance down to 0.18% of total share capital from 0.34%. One older (September 2025) figure put pledged shares at 11.19% of promoter holding, which doesn't obviously reconcile with the 0.18%-of-total-capital figure - these may use different bases, but treat current pledge levels as low-and-declining with moderate rather than high confidence pending the latest exchange filing. No widely-tracked marquee investor (e.g., a well-known FII or LIC in size) was confirmed on the register in available data - if you were expecting a famous name here, it does not show up clearly in what could be verified.
strengths: Consolidated PAT rose 21% YoY to ₹771 crore in Q2 FY27 on record revenue of roughly ₹16,700 crore (+43% YoY)
Net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.51x from 1.71x the previous quarter, with net debt/equity at just 0.32
Angul plant capacity nearly doubled (6 to 12 MTPA), taking group capacity to 15.6 MTPA, with CARE and ICRA both upgrading the credit rating to AA+ in 2026
Promoter pledge is low and falling - down to 0.18% of total capital in June 2026 from 0.34% previously
watchpoints: EBITDA margin slipped to roughly 15% from 16% a year ago as coking coal costs rose, and management has guided a further $20-25/tonne increase for Q3 FY27
Return ratios (ROE 8.2%, ROCE 9.7%) are modest against a P/E of roughly 33x, so the valuation depends on the capacity expansion delivering a real earnings step-up
Stock is down 19.2% from its April 2026 peak of ₹1,286.50, and its 1-year return of +0.72% has lagged steel peer JSW Steel's +10.14%
Promoter pledge figures are inconsistent across sources (0.18% of total capital vs. an older 11.19% of promoter holding) - worth confirming against the latest BSE/NSE shareholding filing
analysis.one_thing: Q3 FY27 EBITDA/tonne and the coking coal cost trajectory - this will show whether the current margin compression is a temporary cost shock or a more structural squeeze on the capacity-expansion payoff.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q2 FY27 results, net debt/EBITDA, capacity figures, credit rating upgrades, and the Sept-2026 shareholding pattern across Business Standard, Screener.in, EquityBulls and company press releases - these were broadly consistent. Not reconciled: FY26 adjusted EBITDA (₹9,099 cr vs ₹9,704 cr depending on source), P/E (32-38.5x range across aggregators), EV/EBITDA (12.8x vs 14.08x), and promoter pledge percentage (0.18% of total capital per a June 2026 disclosure vs. an older 11.19%-of-promoter-holding figure). Could not directly access the company's own investor presentation PDF, so figures rely on financial media and aggregator sources rather than the primary filing. No confirmed Q3 FY27 results date was found.
